title: The Middleware Pipeline
blurb: Order the app.Use*() calls so the request reaches its endpoint. Order is everything here — and getting it wrong fails in very specific ways.

glossary.UseExceptionHandler: Catches unhandled exceptions thrown anywhere downstream and turns them into a clean error response. To cover the whole pipeline it must wrap everything, so it sits at the very top.
glossary.UseHsts: Sends the Strict-Transport-Security header, telling browsers to only ever use HTTPS for this site. Runs very early, right after the exception handler (it's skipped in development).
glossary.UseHttpsRedirection: Redirects any plain-HTTP request to HTTPS. Runs early so everything after it only deals with secure requests.
glossary.UseStaticFiles: Serves files like CSS, JS, and images straight from disk and short-circuits the pipeline. Placed before routing and auth so a public asset doesn't pay for routing or demand a login.
glossary.UseRouting: Matches the request to an endpoint and attaches its metadata. Anything that needs to know *which* endpoint was selected (CORS, authorization) must come after this.
glossary.UseCors: Applies the Cross-Origin Resource Sharing policy. Runs after routing so it can read the selected endpoint's CORS policy, and before authentication/authorization.
glossary.UseAuthentication: Works out *who* the user is — reads the cookie or token and builds their identity. Must run before authorization, which needs that identity.
glossary.UseAuthorization: Decides *whether* the user is allowed to hit this endpoint. It needs both the endpoint (from routing) and the identity (from authentication), so it comes after both.
glossary.UseEndpoints: Executes the matched endpoint — your controller action. It's the terminal step, so it goes last.

levels.title: L1 · The first four
levels.prompt: Drag these four into the order the request actually runs them. The packet walks top-to-bottom.

failStates.title: Authorized before routing
failStates.explain: Authorization ran before routing selected an endpoint — so there was no endpoint metadata yet, and nothing for it to authorize. UseRouting must come first.

failStates.title: Endpoint ran unguarded
failStates.explain: The endpoint executed before authorization could run, so a protected action fired for an unauthorized request. Authorization has to sit between routing and the endpoint.

failStates.title: Exception handler isn't outermost
failStates.explain: UseExceptionHandler needs to wrap everything downstream. Placed below routing, an exception thrown further along the pipeline escapes it and the client gets a raw 500.

levels.title: L2 · Static files & identity
levels.prompt: A real pipeline adds HTTPS redirection, static files, and authentication. Order all seven.

failStates.title: Authorized before authenticating
failStates.explain: Authorization decided whether the user is allowed before authentication established who the user even is. Authenticate first (set the identity), then authorize against it.

failStates.title: Static file blocked by auth
failStates.explain: Static files sit before auth so a public CSS/JS/image is served straight from disk. Behind authorization, every static asset would demand a login it never needed.

failStates.title: Authorized before routing
failStates.explain: No endpoint is selected until UseRouting runs, so authorization had no endpoint metadata to check. Routing must precede authorization.

levels.title: L3 · The full pipeline
levels.prompt: The canonical production pipeline, including HSTS and CORS. Nine tiles — order them all.

failStates.title: CORS before routing
failStates.explain: CORS runs after routing so it can read the endpoint's CORS policy/metadata. Placed before UseRouting, there's no selected endpoint and a preflight can't be matched to its policy.

failStates.title: Authorized before authenticating
failStates.explain: Authentication must establish the identity before authorization can judge it. Reversed, every request looks anonymous to the authorization check.

failStates.title: Static file blocked by auth
failStates.explain: Static files belong before auth so public assets are served without a login challenge they never required.

failStates.title: Authorized before routing
failStates.explain: Routing selects the endpoint; only then does authorization have metadata to act on. Routing comes first.
